top.title: Seville’s Passionate ‘Gran Derbi’ Divides A City Looking To The Future
top.description: Pablo Fornals of Real Betis celebrates a goal against Sevilla at the Pizjuán last November. Europa Press via Getty Images The last time Real Betis visited Sevilla’s Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán for ‘ El Gran Derbi ’, the game was stopped for more than 15 minutes. Betis won 2-0 that afternoon in November 2025, with second-half goals from Pablo Fornals and Sergi Altimira. Sevilla striker Isaac Romero was sent off and objects thrown from the stands forced the referee to halt play. On Saturday evening, at 6:30pm local time, the Seville derby goes back to Nervión. It is the 13th round of LaLiga, but in Seville nobody treats it as one game among 38. “Here in Seville, football is a way of life, like a religion,” Álvaro Valles told me in a LALIGA press event this week. The Betis goalkeeper was born just outside the city and came through the club’s academy. A rivalry older than LaLiga Sevilla were founded in 1890 while Betis came later, out of a split at Sevilla, and in 1914 a merger created Real Betis Balompié. The first Seville derby was played on October 8, 1915, and Sevilla won it 4-3, and the two side have now met 145 times in official competition. Sevilla lead the record with 66 wins, but have failed to win any of the last three. After November’s heated affair, the return game at La Cartuja in March finished 2-2, after Betis led 2-0 at half time and Alexis Sánchez and Isaac Romero brought Sevilla level. “More than three points” What sets the derby apart is that both clubs carry national weight from the same city. “These are two powerful clubs at national level, and the rivalry is huge,” Valles told international media. “Having two nationally important clubs in the city of Seville makes this match very important all over the world.” Alvaro Valles of Real Betis gestures during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis Balompie at BVB Stadion Dortmund. Getty Images Valles has a useful comparison, as Betis are in the Champions League this season, and he has already played at Borussia Dortmund, with a trip to Bayern Munich to come in January. Asked how those atmospheres compare with a Seville derby, he said they are not alike. “A derby is a one-off game. I always say it doesn’t matter what form either team is in. It’s like a final,” he says. “They’re still worth three points like any other game, but against your eternal rival they’re more than three points. It’s the pride of a whole city.” He has lived the rivalry since childhood as Valles grew up in La Rinconada, left the Betis academy to make his name at UD Las Palmas, and came back to the club in 2025 after spending a year in the stands to see out his contract and ensure a move back to his boyhood club. He calls the return “a dream I had wanted to fulfil since I was a kid: playing at home, in my city, for the club of my life.” Two homes in flux The stadiums that built this rivalry are both about to change. top.title: Manchester United rival Liverpool for Italy international defender as club also informed of former midfielder's potential 2027 return
top.description: Atalanta BC v Parma Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are rivalling Liverpool for Italy international centre-back Giorgio Scalvini as they plan for life after Lisandro Martinez. The Old Trafford hierarchy have also been alerted to a possible 2027 reunion with former midfielder Scott McTominay amid contract talks at Napoli. Recruitment chiefs scout defensive targets According to TEAMtalk , United are carrying out detailed scouting work on Scalvini as they prepare to reinforce up front, at left-back and in central defence. The Italian has caught the eye of several recruitment departments and could become a major defensive target in 2027, either in January or next summer. That search comes as Martinez enters the final months of his deal, despite a one-year club option. Agent chief questions Barcelona interest Speculation surrounding Martinez's future has gathered pace following earlier claims from the outlet that Barcelona admire the Argentine defender, alongside reports in Spain suggesting he is open to listening to an offer from the Liga giants. However, the president of the Spanish Association of Football Agents, Pedro Bravo, has poured cold water on any potential switch to Catalonia. Addressing the transfer rumours, Bravo said: "Lisandro, as far as I'm aware, neither Deco nor [Hansi] Flick are keen on him." He added that the message coming from Flick and sporting director Deco regarding Martinez is clear: "He's a good player, but we don't like him. He doesn't fit in with us." Regardless of Barcelona's stance, Martinez's contract situation still points towards an Old Trafford exit in the near future. Scottish playmaker considers English comeback Alongside their defensive planning, the report states that former United midfielder McTominay is seriously weighing up a return to the Premier League in 2027. His previous employers have already been notified of the opportunity to bring the academy graduate back to Manchester, and club officials have not dismissed the prospect. The publication's sources believe Napoli remain hopeful of keeping the Scotland international in Serie A, with his current agreement set to expire in 18 months. Because the two parties are currently far apart in contract negotiations, intermediaries have begun pushing him towards potential landing spots in case no middle ground can be found. Injury recovery dictates winter timing Timing will play a decisive role in how United approach both pursuits over the coming months. Because Scalvini has only recently returned from injury, a January move may arrive too soon, meaning United and Liverpool will keep tracking his form before deciding when to bid. Meanwhile, McTominay's ongoing standoff in Italy will determine whether a 2027 reunion becomes a concrete option.

top.title: Stephen A. Smith says there’s one rule stopping him from running for President
top.description: Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Sports analyst Stephen A. Smith gives an update on whether he will try to become the next US President. Over the years, Stephen A. Smith has built an impressive fan following thanks to his unfiltered takes on the NBA and NFL. So much so that Smith has now expanded his coverage to things outside of sports, including politics in the United States of America. There have been times when the ESPN analyst has contemplated running for president, but Smith has seemingly given up on that dream. Stephen A. Smith explains why he will not run for US President During a recent podcast appearance with NBA legend Kevin Garnett, Smith talked about a plethora of things. Soon, the conversation shifted to if the ESPN on-air talent wants to run for president. Well, Smith has shut the door on any possibility and it’s because of one important rule. “Listen, would I give all of this up to be the President of the United States of America? Yes, I would. Would I give it up to campaign for the president? H___ no. And according to the rules, you have to give up everything. What they say is you’ve got to give up your money because, by virtue of what I do, let me tell you this: there’s something with the FCC called ‘the equal-time rule,” Smith said. He added, “And equal time means that because of what I do and because I’m on the air all the time, the minute I announce that I’m running, I have to come off the air and give up my career and the money that comes with it. “Now, that ain’t happening, dog. That’s not happening.” Running for president doesn’t automatically mean that Smith will win the election, and if he fails, he could lose relevance among fans. An overnight flight from Cincinnati to Manchester took Pochettino from his post-match duties after the United States’ win over Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning to United’s Carrington complex, where he has quickly got to work ahead of Sunday’s clash with old rivals Liverpool. Pochettino has been linked with United’s top job before but, while he takes over with the club in the bottom three having won only one Premier League match all season, the 54-year-old believes he is better placed for the Old Trafford challenge now than ever before. “Of course we were missing [club football], we were missing it a lot,” he said. “I think we are animals of the grass. top.title: Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA
top.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal. On Saturday CA gave its "unanimous support" to Cummins, and he said he would take part in the independent forum set up for players and staff. Cummins has faced claims to step down as captain after Cameron Bancroft's detailed testimony supported claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. CA and Cummins met this week, with the former saying it was "determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn". "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," CA said. "We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised." CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said Cummins has been an "exemplary leader" in his five years as captain. "He has consistently spoken and articulated what happened back in 2018 in his version of events. Nothing's changed. Thus, nothing's changing with our captaincy," Greenberg told BBC Sport. Greenberg acknowledged that people's version of events "directly contradict" each other but said Cummins has "not moved one inch" from his story, giving the same account now as he did when interviewed the day after the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins is due to lead Australia in the opening match of a four-Test series against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth. The pace bowler reiterated his stance that he had no involvement in or knowledge of the sandpaper plot during a 68-minute news conference last week. Cummins has said he will attend the forum that has been set up by CA for players and staff to share their version of events. "I support the forum 100%. I will be there," he said. "All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. "There will be a lot of difficult conversations, but that is what's needed. "Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority." The row over the sandpaper saga, one of the biggest controversies in Test history, has engulfed Australian sport since Khawaja's claims emerged two weeks ago. In 2018 Bancroft was banned for nine months and captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner for a year after Bancroft was caught rubbing sandpaper on the ball during the third Test at Newlands. top.title: An Australian captain who can play for Wales in 2027
top.description: Liam Wright had to wait four years between his fifth and six caps for Australia [Getty Images] Ospreys flanker and once-Australian captain Liam Wright will be at the Principality Stadium today to watch the Wallabies take on Wales in Cardiff. Wright knows that in less than a year, it is possible he could be playing for Australia or Wales at the World Cup in the land of his birth. The 29-year-old has made six appearances for the Wallabies, but his previous game was in July 2024. So despite being capped by the Wallabies, World Rugby regulations would allow him to play for another country three years after his previous international appearance. His eligibility to switch allegiances would start next summer, and just a few months before the World Cup begins in Australia in September 2027. Wright has Welsh heritage, with his grandfather hailing from Pembroke Dock. After more than a year out of professional rugby, Wright moved 12,000 miles to join Ospreys and wants to return to the international stage. "Test rugby is what I want to get to; it's the pinnacle and where I want to play and end up again," he said. Will an international return be for Australia or Wales? Liam Wright played in the back row for Australia against Wales in July 2024 [Getty Images] Which country Wright might play for remains to be seen. When asked about potentially representing Wales, he replied: "I imagine myself playing Test rugby and wanting to do it in a gold jersey, but I'm not going to turn down opportunities anywhere. "If the door is closed for the Wallabies and I'm playing good enough and Wales do come knocking, I'd definitely explore it. "I want to get back playing Test footy [rugby] and play for the Wallabies, but fate has a weird way of working where we've landed in Wales. "I've now got to explore the heritage. I was going past Pembroke Dock the other week and stayed there in an Airbnb and explored the area a bit, which is where my grandfather's from. "Things have a funny way of working out, so I won't rule anything out." Wright will be mindful that Wales and Australia have impressive back-row resources at their disposal. Wales head coach Steve Tandy told the Scrum V podcast in October he had not talked to Wright, who met up with the Australian camp in Cardiff this week. Australia head coach Les Kiss knows Wright well from their Queensland days. "We will always keep an eye on someone of his calibre," said Kiss. "The big thing for Liam was getting back into the game, and I've worked closely with him at the Reds for a number of years. "He was in that gym, in the physio room, throwing everything to get that shoulder right. "I loved the look in his eyes this week. He looked happy again, getting out there, plying his trade and loving the sense of living in a different environment. "I was happy to catch up with him and see how he feels good about himself again." nigeria.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
nigeria.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. nigeria.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
nigeria.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports. Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations. nigeria.title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
nigeria.description: Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie. The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for. nigeria.title: UNICEF raises alarm over 624,000 out-of-school children
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised concerns over the high number of out-of-school children in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states, disclosing that about 624,000 children have been identified as being outside the classroom across the three states. The organisation said although about 68,000 children had benefited from interventions to return them to school, the scale of the challenge required urgent government action, increased investment and stronger community mobilisation. UNICEF’s Chief of Field Office in Sokoto, Dr Michael Juma, made this known at a media briefing organised by the organisation’s Sokoto Field Office as part of activities marking the 2026 World Children’s Day. He called for coordinated action by governments, media organisations, traditional institutions, religious leaders and community stakeholders to address challenges confronting children in the region. Juma urged journalists across the three states to intensify public enlightenment, investigative reporting and advocacy to promote children’s rights, strengthen government accountability and ensure access to education, healthcare, nutrition and other essential services. Describing the media as a critical partner in advancing children’s rights, he said journalists must go beyond reporting events to exposing gaps in service delivery and holding relevant authorities accountable. “The media are important duty-bearers in advancing children’s rights. Journalists must provide balanced coverage that highlights development achievements while drawing attention to persistent gaps affecting the wellbeing of children,” he said. He reaffirmed UNICEF’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with the governments of Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara, development partners, traditional and religious leaders, and grassroots organisations to guarantee children access to quality and inclusive education, healthcare, adequate nutrition, safe drinking water and social protection. Providing an account of interventions undertaken through UNICEF’s partnerships with the three state governments, Juma disclosed that approximately 98,000 children had benefited from the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) programme, designed to improve foundational literacy and numeracy. He said the organisation was also supporting teacher professional development, provision of instructional materials, accelerated basic education, integrated Qur’anic education and innovative learning opportunities, including radio-based education and the Nigeria Learning Passport. According to him, the interventions are particularly targeted at children affected by insecurity, displacement and other emergencies. On healthcare and immunisation, Juma disclosed that approximately 7.8 million children across the three states had been reached through measles-rubella vaccination, while more than five million children were vaccinated during the last concluded polio immunisation campaign. Thank you for showing up. The love has been organic, and we feel every bit of it,” Lancelot said. The premiere of “Issakaba Returns” was spectacular and memorable. Drummers, dancers and chanting fans set the mood, recreating the fearless spirit of the Issakaba Boys who, 25 years ago, stood against evil in the South-East. nigeria.title: Davido and Chioma: The love story continues
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company. It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the studio, borrowing a leaf from the likes of Adekunle Gold and Simi, Banky W and Adesuwa Etomi, as well as Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who have all turned their love stories into music. For Davido, Chioma has never just been his wife. She has been his muse from the very beginning. Their love story in music started in 2018 with ‘Assurance’, the birthday gift Davido dedicated to Chioma when they were still dating. Chioma starred in the video, and the song became one of the most iconic love anthems in Afrobeats history. She returned in 2020 for ‘1 Milli’, whose wedding-themed video further celebrated their relationship. Nearly eight years after ‘Assurance’, ‘Already Falling’ brings that story full circle, from young lovers to husband and wife. The song, the eighth track on Davido’s sixth studio album, “ORIADÉ”, was released on July 31, 2026. It blends English, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, and reimagines Elvis Presley’s timeless classic ‘Can’t Help Falling in Love’ through an Afrobeats lens with background vocals by Peruzz The official video, released on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, stars Chioma as his leading lady once again. Directed by Meji Alabi, who also directed ‘Assurance, the video was filmed at the historic Château de Chanteloup, the estate of French cognac house Maison Martell in Cognac, France. It blends French elegance with Nigerian style, with Davido arriving in a horse-drawn carriage, serenading Chioma in grand interiors, and later recreating a proposal scene by a lake at dusk, where he goes down on one knee to present her with a ring. Though the couple wedded in a lavish Lagos ceremony in June 2024, the proposal scene is a cinematic metaphor for renewed commitment, not a new engagement. Davido announced the release himself with the caption: “Already Falling. From us to you. Enjoy.” Like other music stars, Davido is proving that a real-life love story can become a powerful artistic brand. For fans, ‘Already Falling’ is more than a music video. It is a continuation of a story they have followed since 2018 ; from young lovers, to husband and wife, to parents, told in Davido’s most personal songs. And with Chioma by his side in the studio, on screen, and on tour, including their recent high-profile trip to Tanzania with Diamond Platnumz, the couple shows no signs of slowing down. nigeria.title: Soludo approves N50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved a N50,000 December bonus for civil servants in the state, with the payment expected to reflect in their December 2026 salaries. The governor announced the bonus during the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka, where he also approved measures to improve the working environment and productivity of civil servants. Soludo acknowledged the economic challenges facing workers, admitting that their current salaries were inadequate amid prevailing economic conditions. He, however, assured the workers that his administration would only make financial commitments it could realistically fulfil. “I understand the situation and economic conditions, that we need to be able to do something. The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it. “But there is one thing I also want to tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour,” he said. Addressing comparisons between Anambra’s salary structure and those of other states, the governor urged civil servants to consider the different revenue bases and economic capacities of state governments before making such assessments. He stressed that sustainable governance and responsible financial management, rather than unfulfilled promises, remained the guiding principles of his administration. Soludo also expressed appreciation to the workers for their support during last year’s governorship election, saying he was pleased that public servants overwhelmingly voted for his administration in recognition of its developmental efforts. Responding to three major requests presented by the workers at the event, the governor immediately directed the rehabilitation of roads within the secretariat complex, approved the establishment of an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Centre and authorised the pruning of overgrown trees across the premises. Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Barr. Ngozi Iwouno, commended Soludo for restoring security and normalcy across the state. She said civil servants could now attend work regularly without fear, noting that the disruption previously caused by Monday sit-at-home orders had been overcome. Iwouno said the improved security situation had restored confidence among workers and enabled them to discharge their duties more consistently. nigeria.title: Passengers fear proposed biometric checks may cause chaos at domestic airports
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more difficult. They insisted that the plan appeared rushed and had not been properly thought through, particularly as the festive travel season would still be ongoing when the policy takes effect. They also feared that its implementation could trigger a repeat of the chaos that followed the introduction of the Go Cashless payment system, which caused hours of gridlock at airports in Lagos and Abuja. In March, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, introduced an electronic payment system known as Go Cashless at the toll gate of two of the country’s busiest airports. Its rollout left passengers travelling through the airports in Lagos and Abuja stranded for hours, triggering massive gridlock, missed flights and widespread frustration. While some travellers abandoned their vehicles at airport entrances after encountering difficulties completing payments, others said they missed scheduled flights after spending hours trying to gain access to the airports. The disruption prompted President Bola Tinubu to order the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, to announce a suspension of the system on the fourth day of its implementation. With the busy Yuletide travel period extending into January, passengers and industry observers fear that a similar situation could unfold at the Lagos airport, the country’s busiest, especially as Keyamo has given domestic airlines until December 31, 2026, to integrate their operations with the system that will facilitate the biometric checks. Keyamo warned that airlines that fail to comply with the directive would not be allowed to board passengers from January 1, 2027. Known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, v-PASS, the biometric identity verification system is linked to the National Identification Number, NIN, of Nigerians. It is designed exclusively for domestic flights, with all passengers required to provide their NIN during check-in. Passengers are also expected to pay additional charges for the service. Speaking during the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Keyamo said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it. nigeria.title: Pa Fasoranti for burial Dec 17; Ondo govt unveils 8-day programme
nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, AKURE The Ondo State Government has released an eight-day programme of burial activities for the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, CFR, with his funeral service and interment scheduled for Thursday, December 17, 2026. The programme, signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the State Burial Committee, Dr Kayode Ajulo and Apostle Eniola Olushola, Esq, respectively, shows that the ceremonies will begin on Sunday, December 13, with a cultural heritage day in honour of the deceased, who was born on May 11, 1926 and died on October 20, 2026. The opening ceremony, scheduled for 12 noon, will feature a showcase of Ondo State’s cultural heritage at the Dr Olusegun Mimiko International Centre for Culture and Events (The Dome), Akure. A commendation service will hold at Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, at 9.00 am on Monday, December 14, followed by a novelty football match in Fasoranti’s honour at the Akure Township Stadium. The football fixtures will see Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, take on St Frances, Akure, at 2.00 pm, while Akure High School will face Ondo Boys High School at 4.00 pm. Activities on Tuesday, December 15, will feature a symposium, national tribute and academic award at The Dome, Akure. The symposium, themed “A Selfless Cradle Light That The Yoruba Race Can’t Forget In A Hurry”, will be organised by Afenifere, the DAWN Commission and the Ondo State Government. It is scheduled for 10.00 am and will be followed by a national tribute and academic award. A lying-in-state and Christian wake-keep will take place at the deceased’s country home, Omolere Close, Akure, at 4.00 pm on Wednesday, December 16. The funeral service will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Thursday, December 17, with interment to follow immediately at the church cemetery. A reception and entertainment of guests will subsequently hold at designated venues for the different categories of guests. The programme will continue on Friday, December 18, with a thanksgiving service at Akure Central Mosque at 1.00 pm, while Saturday, December 19, has been set aside for family visits to Baba’s residence. The final activity, an outing and thanksgiving service, will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Sunday, December 20. Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. A rivalry older than LaLiga Sevilla were founded in 1890 while Betis came later, out of a split at Sevilla, and in 1914 a merger created Real Betis Balompié. sports.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal. On Saturday CA gave its "unanimous support" to Cummins, and he said he would take part in the independent forum set up for players and staff. Cummins has faced claims to step down as captain after Cameron Bancroft's detailed testimony supported claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. CA and Cummins met this week, with the former saying it was "determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn". "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," CA said. "We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised." CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said Cummins has been an "exemplary leader" in his five years as captain. "He has consistently spoken and articulated what happened back in 2018 in his version of events. Nothing's changed. Thus, nothing's changing with our captaincy," Greenberg told BBC Sport. Greenberg acknowledged that people's version of events "directly contradict" each other but said Cummins has "not moved one inch" from his story, giving the same account now as he did when interviewed the day after the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins is due to lead Australia in the opening match of a four-Test series against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth. The pace bowler reiterated his stance that he had no involvement in or knowledge of the sandpaper plot during a 68-minute news conference last week. Cummins has said he will attend the forum that has been set up by CA for players and staff to share their version of events. "I support the forum 100%. I will be there," he said. "All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. "There will be a lot of difficult conversations, but that is what's needed. "Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority." The row over the sandpaper saga, one of the biggest controversies in Test history, has engulfed Australian sport since Khawaja's claims emerged two weeks ago. sports.description: Liam Wright had to wait four years between his fifth and six caps for Australia [Getty Images] Ospreys flanker and once-Australian captain Liam Wright will be at the Principality Stadium today to watch the Wallabies take on Wales in Cardiff. Wright knows that in less than a year, it is possible he could be playing for Australia or Wales at the World Cup in the land of his birth. The 29-year-old has made six appearances for the Wallabies, but his previous game was in July 2024. So despite being capped by the Wallabies, World Rugby regulations would allow him to play for another country three years after his previous international appearance. His eligibility to switch allegiances would start next summer, and just a few months before the World Cup begins in Australia in September 2027. Wright has Welsh heritage, with his grandfather hailing from Pembroke Dock. After more than a year out of professional rugby, Wright moved 12,000 miles to join Ospreys and wants to return to the international stage. "Test rugby is what I want to get to; it's the pinnacle and where I want to play and end up again," he said. Will an international return be for Australia or Wales? Liam Wright played in the back row for Australia against Wales in July 2024 [Getty Images] Which country Wright might play for remains to be seen. When asked about potentially representing Wales, he replied: "I imagine myself playing Test rugby and wanting to do it in a gold jersey, but I'm not going to turn down opportunities anywhere. "If the door is closed for the Wallabies and I'm playing good enough and Wales do come knocking, I'd definitely explore it. "I want to get back playing Test footy [rugby] and play for the Wallabies, but fate has a weird way of working where we've landed in Wales. "I've now got to explore the heritage. I was going past Pembroke Dock the other week and stayed there in an Airbnb and explored the area a bit, which is where my grandfather's from. "Things have a funny way of working out, so I won't rule anything out." Wright will be mindful that Wales and Australia have impressive back-row resources at their disposal. Wales head coach Steve Tandy told the Scrum V podcast in October he had not talked to Wright, who met up with the Australian camp in Cardiff this week. sports.title: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it?
sports.description: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it? Serie A has several underdog stories blossoming this season on both team and player levels and is all the more worthwhile for it. One such story is of Gustavo Varela, who despite being in his debut season in Italy already looks like a man on a mission. Having scored just seven goals last season in 33 appearances while on loan at Gil Vicente from Benfica, the 21-year-old already has 11 goals in 11 outings this term. These are numbers few were expecting, that too for a team not expected to have a great campaign. Monza are again looking down the barrel, and between their early-season slump and several of their counterparts looking keen to at least put up a fight, things are not looking good for the Brianzoli. But Varela is unquestionably a shining light. Even if he doesn’t manage to help keep Monza up, he is turning enough heads to be able to earn himself a move and not have to try his luck in Serie B. Some even believe a mid-season switch to not be out of question. It would make sense if Monza were to capitalise on his hype knowing they might go down anyway, and there’s previous for this. But is it too soon for Varela? Is he really already worth €40 million. Despite market valuations, the price of a player comes down to however much the buying party is willing to conjure up. And while there are several success stories featuring players who move early and thrive, there are several others — often more frequent — of players who move too early and for too lofty a price tag which they never manage to justify. In recent years alone there are several cautionary tales. Krzysztof Piątek, case in point, looked like the next great striker of his generation before moving to Milan after just half a season with Genoa, and while his numbers mostly remain respectable, the now Al-Duhail man never reached the heights that were expected of him during his short stint at the Marassi. Similarly, Juan Manuel Iturbe, a darling of the video game folk, arrived at Roma amid much fanfare before his career plateaued. After struggling in Europe, he has gone on to have a respectable career in the Americas and is currently at his boyhood club, Cerro Porteño. In fact, one could even argue that Juventus that did not quite get what they were hoping for when they splurged €70 million on Dušan Vlahović to pry him away from Fiorentina in January 2022. All that said, the fact of the matter remains that the current market is a fidgeting, impatient one. technology.title: NASA Mars rover and orbiter suffer glitches
technology.description: It's been a bad few weeks for technology on and off the planet, as NASA reported problems with its Perseverance Mars rover and Odyssey orbiter this week. For Perseverance, the problem seems to be a relatively straightforward communications issue that has paused science operations because of low data rates. The Odyssey orbiter, however, is facing an issue that could end the mission. The 2001 Mars Odyssey reached orbit around Mars in October 2001 to search for evidence of water and ice on the surface. The mission was supposed to last two and a half years, but the spacecraft's operations have been extended for a quarter of a century. In that time, it has had its fair share of ups and downs, including the failure of one of its four reaction wheels in 2013. Three reaction wheels are needed to orient the spacecraft; otherwise, it must fall back to its hydrazine thrusters. Earlier in November, between the 4th and 6th, Odyssey dropped into safe mode, which engineers determined was caused by one of the remaining reaction wheels stopping spinning. Science data stopped flowing as the team worked to recover the component; the good news was that the wheel moved when commanded. The bad news is that if the thrusters need to be used, only a few months of fuel remain. More bad news is that the spacecraft is part of NASA's Mars Relay Network, and was responsible for sending back the first post-landing images from the Phoenix lander and the Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity rovers. Its loss (should it come to that) would therefore be keenly felt. In the event the orbiter is indeed approaching the end of the road, the European Space Agency's Mars Express (MEX) and Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) could pick up some of the load although, as a former ESA insider put it: "MEX is a science mission that can do relay where TGO is a relay mission that also does science." According to NASA, TGO already sends the most relay data from Mars to Earth. The challenge facing the Perseverance trundlebot is one of communication. On October 30, the rover's main computer detected problems with the primary radio (a series of "heartbeats" from the device did not arrive as expected) and automatically switched to a redundant backup, placing itself in a protective safe mode. So far, so expected. Engineers brought the rover back from safe mode, analyzed the data, and made an unpleasant discovery. The backup radio was not performing as it should – it was operating at approximately half of its expected power output. Both radios were therefore deemed inoperable – at least until the team has got to the bottom of the issues – and the rover has used X-band communications over its high-gain antenna to talk to Earth ever since. The problem here is that the connection provides a significantly lower data rate, meaning science and instrument operations are on hold. Engineers are working first to return the backup radio to operational status, then to address the primary. ®

Meanwhile, AWS Marketplace has opened its door to bot-based buying. "Buying software and data through AWS Marketplace just got easier, for you and for the AI agents working alongside you," said Mya Papolu, product marketing manager for AWS Marketplace and Partner Services at Amazon Web Services, in a blog post this week. "For re:Invent 2026, we’re launching capabilities designed to reduce friction across the buying journey." For a company that has blocked bots from Google, Meta, and OpenAI, and sued Perplexity to keep its AI-encumbered Comet browser away, the openness of AWS Marketplace to agentic commerce invites questions. We asked Amazon to explain but we've not heard back. AWS Marketplace is allowing AI agents to scour its site and buy some cloud software products using the x402 agentic payment protocol , which is supported by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments. Introduced by Coinbase and Cloudflare , x402 got handed over to the Linux Foundation earlier this year, and now has support from a variety of tech platforms, including AWS, Google, Stripe, and various blockchain networks. About a week ago, Brave Software announced support for x402 payments through its search API. AWS requires sellers to register with AWS Marketplace and to integrate the AWS Marketplace x402 SDK to enable agentic product purchases. Transactions settle in USD through AWS billing so existing spending controls can be applied. And now, customers in the US can buy some AWS Marketplace software without an AWS account; instead they're asked to provide an email or social media login, and a credit card. While AWS Marketplace today lists mainly familiar software categories (Business Applications, Data & Analytics, DevOps, Infrastructure Software, and so on), AWS has a broader product inventory in mind. Beyond software and APIs, the biz sees a future in selling content and data. Papolu announced that AWS is now selling " data as a service ." "Data providers can list their offerings in AWS Marketplace, making commercial data accessible to both human teams and the agents working alongside them via the AWS Marketplace website, APIs, and MCP server," she said. This includes services like Moody's Credit MCP server for financial research; Reuters Geopolitical News for AI-structured reporting; US Building Permits, Contractors & Residents Data from Shovels; and US-EN Multi-Speaker Conversational Acoustic Corpus from Uber AI Solutions. In canned remarks provided to AWS, Nandhan Puppala, general manager at Uber AI Solutions, said that data quality and readiness can help advance AI products. technology.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
technology.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. All three financial firms attributed the compromises to a third-party provider, and while nothing in the stolen files name the vendor, the timing matches up with a Qubole supply-chain campaign disclosed earlier this month by Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders and AI data security company Sentra. technology.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
technology.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. technology.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
technology.description: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. technology.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
technology.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.
technology.description: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing : The pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts. CTIA said the pilot test shows "that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications." technology.description: In a swirl of questions, fears, and outrage, the US Army announced Thursday that it would delay a plan to blow up 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide, which would launch toxic gas and lead into the air. A federal appeals court further halted plans later on Thursday with an emergency order. The plume, containing neurotoxic lead, could potentially drift 100 miles north of the Army installation housing it in Middletown, Iowa, according to modeling released by the Army earlier this week. The Army had planned to carry out two controlled detonations, set off simultaneously around noon Friday, to destroy the barrels where they lie, which is in earth-covered concrete containment structures (called earth-covered magazines or ECMs). Prior to the court stay, the Army rescheduled the blast until November 23 to provide more time to communicate about the situation with Iowans, who have reported being unaware of the detonations until earlier this week. science.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers.
